title: Scrap-fed EAF steel installation, CN 7213.10, calendar year 2026
purpose: One set of inputs and one set of answers, read by both calculation engines. Neither engine owns it. See docs/fixtures/README.md.
regulatoryBasis: Regulation (EU) 2023/956, Annex II - iron & steel is charged on direct emissions only

processEmissions.conversionFactorSource: EU MRR (EU) 2018/2066 - tCO2 per tC from molar masses 44.010 / 12.011

exposure.status: BOTH INPUTS UNRESOLVED - spec 9. The arithmetic is pinned here so a later change to an engine cannot move it silently; the two numbers themselves are placeholders and must not be quoted to a customer.

backend.status: COVERED - the backend reproduces all four emission lines of this fixture: fuel combustion through a net calorific value, process emissions through a mass balance, indirect electricity, and precursors including multi-tier chains. What it still does not do is listed under `unsupported`, and none of it is an emission line.
mapping: Precursor quantities are ABSOLUTE TONNES in the backend request and PER TONNE OF OUTPUT in the fixture, so each is multiplied by production: scrap 1.08 x 10500 = 11340 t, pig iron 0.05 x 10500 = 525 t. The backend then divides by production again, so the contribution is identical - this is a change of units, not of arithmetic. Below the top level the backend uses TNE_PER_TNE, the same ratio the fixture states.

The fuel row travels in its metered unit with the calorific value beside it (148800 MTQ x 0.0383 GJ_PER_MTQ), never pre-converted by the caller: the conversion that most often goes wrong belongs inside the audit trace, not upstream of it.

The backend returns decimal STRINGS at 80 significant digits. `covered` below is asserted as exact decimal equality. `coveredWithinTolerance` is asserted against `tolerance`, and only for lines where the shared expectation is itself a rounded figure - 319.7161 is the display form of 319.716144, and no engine can equal it exactly without being wrong.

closed.how: GJ, the metered units MTQ/KGM/LTR/TNE and their GJ_PER_* calorific values were added to UnitCode, and SourceStreamInput gained net_calorific_value. A quantity in a metered unit with no calorific value is refused rather than converted with a standard value, mirroring toGJ in certrace-portal/lib/cbam/units.ts.
closed.guard: POST a metered quantity with no net_calorific_value - it must be refused with CALORIFIC_VALUE_REQUIRED, and GJ together with a calorific value with CALORIFIC_VALUE_NOT_APPLICABLE.

closed.how: ProcessEmissionInput with its own MASS_BALANCE trace method, carrying CO2_PER_C = 3.664 as an engine constant with its source rather than as a caller-supplied emission factor.
closed.guard: The trace for the electrode row must say MASS_BALANCE and name CO2_PER_C with its regulatory source.

closed.how: PrecursorInput gained children and own_process_specific_emissions, resolved depth-first: SEE(n) = ownProcess(n) + sum over children of qty x SEE(child), with scrap short-circuiting to zero. Mirrors seeForNode in certrace-portal/lib/cbam/precursor-tree.ts, including the rule that a node with children ignores its own declared figure.
closed.guard: A cycle must be refused with PRECURSOR_CYCLE and a chain deeper than 10 tiers with PRECURSOR_DEPTH_EXCEEDED - the same cap as MAX_PRECURSOR_DEPTH in the portal.

unsupported.reason: materialMix reports scrapRatio over total input mass, which is a different question from the mass-balance yield the portal shows. Neither is wrong; they are simply not the same number and must not be compared. The backend's masses cover top-level precursors only, because everything deeper is a ratio per tonne of its parent rather than a weight.

Formulas 5 and 6 are commercial, not MRV: per-buyer allocation and certificate exposure depend on shipment records and a certificate price, neither of which the calculation API is given. They live only in the portal today. Listed here so that nobody reads their absence from the backend as an oversight.

The portal reads a negative ownProcessSee as zero, because a browser must not throw in the middle of a form. The backend refuses the request instead. Both agree on every valid input; they differ only in what happens to an invalid one, and that difference is deliberate - an audit engine that silently rewrites an input is worse than one that says no.
